subject: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datastream.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-18T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)

Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we want to formalize a short mutual action plan (MAP) that ties the benchmarking run results to a close timeline so your procurement team has the artifacts they need. Proposed high-level plan below; happy to adjust timelines to match your blackout windows.

Ask: confirm test windows and whether your ops team can provide ephemeral API keys for the sandbox env by EOD Tuesday.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Week 0 (this week): exchange test access + finalize test account list.
- Week 1 (Mon–Tue): Redwood runs controlled concurrency sweep (32/64/128) and TTFT spot checks.
- Week 1 (Wed): DataStream runs customer-side validation in shadow mode.
- Week 2 (Thu): Joint review of results, sign-off on performance SLOs, and procurement closes.

Benchmark targets we discussed: latency p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms, TTFT < 450ms at 64 concurrent sessions; sustainable throughput target ~1.5k rps for short bursts. We'll include fallback model variant for sub-100ms median under low concurrency.

I attached a draft MAP (redwood-map-v1.2.pdf) and a short access guide. I can send a test-account bundle once you confirm the right ops contact.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datastream.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@datastream.com, procurement@datastream.com
Date: 2027-01-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)

Ben — thanks, this looks good. Ops can provision sandbox keys but we need the exact endpoint and a short playbook for safely running high-RPS jobs. Procurement also asked for measurable acceptance criteria in the MAP (we'll need p95/p99 and TTFT acceptance numbers spelled out).

Can you provide: 
- exact test endpoints and sample request payloads
- list of model variants you'll test (and quantization profiles)
- suggested load windows in PST (we're available 2027-01-19 02:00–06:00 UTC / 2027-01-20 03:00–07:00 UTC)

Olivia
Olivia Chen | Sr. Platform Engineer, DataStream Inc
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datastream.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-18T12:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)

Olivia — great, below are the specifics you'll need. Laura and Monica are copied with keys and the playbook.

Test endpoints (sandbox):
- Host: https://sandbox-api.redwood.ai/ds-4721/v1/generate
- Ingress token: DS-SANDBOX-XXXX-REDACTED (ops will rotate after tests)
- Example payload: {"input": "<sample prompt>", "max_tokens": 128, "stream": false}

Model variants and profiles we'll run:
- redwood-instruct-3b (fp16, baseline)
- redwood-instruct-3b-q4 (int4 quant, cost-optimized)
- redwood-gen-7b (fp16) — spot-check for throughput headroom

Load matrix (planned runs):
- Concurrency sweep: 32, 64, 96, 128 sessions (sustained 10m per step).
- Burst test: 1800 RPS for 60s.
- TTFT sampling: 500 random requests per run to capture cold-start variance.

Acceptance criteria proposal (for procurement):
- p50 latency <= 80ms at 64 concurrent sessions (redwood-instruct-3b-q4)
- p95 latency <= 300ms at 64 concurrent sessions
- TTFT median <= 450ms across 500 samples
- No correctness regressions vs baseline prompts (we'll include a 50-prompt eval set)

Suggested windows (UTC):
- 2027-01-19 02:00–06:00 UTC (recommended)
- alternate: 2027-01-20 03:00–07:00 UTC

I'll hand off keys and the step-by-step load script to Laura. If those windows work for you, can you ask Ops to drop the sandbox tokens into the access file by EOD tonight so Laura can schedule a dry run?

—Ben
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ops@datastream.com, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datastream.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-18T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)

Hi Ops — attaching the minimal playbook and the exact load harness commands. Please drop the sandbox keys into the shared file (access-instructions-DS.txt). We'll use the following harness parameters (example):

- runner: locust (HTTP scenario)
- target endpoint: https://sandbox-api.redwood.ai/ds-4721/v1/generate
- username: ds_test_account_01
- sample command: locust -f ds_locustfile.py --headless -u 128 -r 16 --run-time 10m --host https://sandbox-api.redwood.ai/ds-4721

Attachments included: access-instructions-DS.txt (contains placeholder tokens) and an abbreviated MAP PDF. After keys are in place we'll do a 10m dry run at 32 concurrency tonight and then the full sweep on the 19th UTC window.

Laura Bennett | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datastream.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-20T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)

Team — ran the full sweep on 2027-01-19 during the primary window. Summary of key metrics (redwood-instruct-3b-q4):
- Concurrency 32: throughput plateau 420 rps, median latency 38ms, p95 110ms, TTFT median 290ms
- Concurrency 64: throughput plateau 900 rps, median latency 62ms, p95 210ms, TTFT median 335ms
- Concurrency 96: throughput plateau 1,250 rps, median latency 95ms, p95 350ms, TTFT median 410ms
- Concurrency 128: overload behaviour observed; errors increased to 2.3% (rate-limited). Sustained throughput ~1,650 rps with p95 > 600ms.

Burst 60s @ 1,800 RPS: short-term plateau achieved but with 3.1% error ratio on the tail; recommend advising ops not to run bursts >1,600 RPS in production without autoscaling buffer.

Attached: ds-scale-run-20270119.csv (full samples), quick notes in the Drive link. We ran the eval set (50 prompts) — no semantic regressions vs baseline. Quantized variant shows ~2.2x cost reduction with modest tail latency increase at very high concurrency.

Next steps:
- Joint review Tuesday 2027-01-21 15:00 UTC to sign the MAP and finalize SLO numbers for procurement.
- Procurement to confirm DocuSign link and final pricing adjustments (Ben).

-Monica
Monica Patel | Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datastream.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@datastream.com>, ops@datastream.com
Date: 2027-01-21T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scale validation & close timeline - DataStream (MAP + test windows)

Thanks — the numbers look good and align with what our SREs expected. Procurement is comfortable with the proposed acceptance criteria but asked for a single-line summary we can put into the purchase order and DocuSign. Suggested PO language (approved internally):

"Redwood Inference to deliver service such that median TTFT <= 350ms and p95 latency <= 300ms at 64 concurrent sessions on the redwood-instruct-3b-q4 model variant in the agreed sandbox; semantic parity checks to pass 95% of the 50-prompt eval set."

We're good to proceed with the DocuSign flow. Ops will coordinate account creation; Ben — can you send the DocuSign link and final MAP PDF so procurement can complete signatures tomorrow?

Olivia
(end of thread)
